title: Open the label-to-figure gate: one more blind annotation of a label-linked folio, or label-locus matching in the agreement rule
statement: P-G-020 asks for two statistics to be registered as facts and checked against a one-table reuse chain. Both are run and both return not-a-number on the manuscript and on the chain alike, because vs/dsl.py pictures() reads only picture items whose read-time verdict is AGREED - a folio reaches AGREED when a second, independent seat annotates it and the two agree on kind and on 80 per cent of shared features - and of the 50 picture items on the record exactly one folio reaches AGREED (f72v1), whose 32 objects carry no label field. Meanwhile the same 50 draft annotations hold 1,395 objects, 683 with a label field, 682 of which name a label line that exists in the text (892 label lines in the book), over 14 folios: f99r 98, f73r 64, f73v 64, f70v2 61, f72v1 60, f72v2 60, f72v3 60, f68r1 58 and others. The data is there; the agreement rule is what excludes it. Either give one of those folios a second blind annotation from a different seat, or match objects by label locus rather than by kind and order when scoring agreement (the route PR #448 proposed and which was closed unmerged, as was #431 which landed the statistics). Then the two registrations filed here become scoreable and the control means something: a chain writing the text has no access to the drawings, so it should fail label_in_page_text where the manuscript passes. Until that asymmetry is shown, P-G-006's remaining question cannot be answered and no further invented language should be designed - none of the languages filed so far predicts a label fact, because none was registrable.
check: A picture item on a folio that already holds a draft annotation, from a different seat and blind, reaching AGREED with at least 10 objects whose label field names a label line; then fact.json for label_in_page_text and feature_label_share scored on the hidden pages, and the same two statistics run on a one-table reuse chain's text laid onto the same pages, reported together.
